name: Dr. Elaine Ingham
bio:
Dr. Elaine Ingham served as the Soil Food Web School’s Founder, Principal Ambassador, and Science and Research Advisor. Dr. Ingham began her college career at St. Olaf College, where she graduated cum laude with a Bachelor of Arts. She earned her Master of Science in Marine Biology from Texas A&M and her Ph.D. in Soil Microbiology from Colorado State in 1981. From there, she completed her post-doc at the University of Georgia Institute of Ecology before serving as an Instructor and later an Associate Professor for many years at Oregon State University. During her travels, she served as the first President of the Soil Ecology Society, the Program Director for the Ecological Society of America, and a member of the American Society of Microbiology. In addition to starting Soil Foodweb Inc. 26 years ago, Dr. Ingham owned and then sold the Soil Foodweb Institute in Australia and served as Chief Scientist at the Rodale Institute. Dr. Ingham’s research is global, and her scientific papers date as far back as 1982, with research concerning ultraviolet-induced autofluorescence of arbuscular mycorrhizal root infections. Seventy-six papers later, she focused on milk comparison between organic and conventional farms in the United States. Dr. Ingham has written 6 book chapters for published books, participated in research teams publishing 17 technical reports, and has been a speaker at agricultural conferences in Great Britain, Brazil, Australia, and numerous states throughout America. Dr. Ingham served as the global leader in the Soil Food Web sciences and is highly respected worldwide for her achievements. In 2019, she teamed up with Luke Louka and created The Soil Food Web School (SFWS).

Dr. Ingham passed in 2026, and the Soil Food Web Foundation exists to further her legacy.

name: Kavi Reddy
bio: Kavi Reddy is a community organizer, regenerative designer, and permaculture educator focused on advancing ecological resilience and food system transformation. Her career spans permaculture farms, non-profits, startups, and venture capital firms in the U.S. and India. Kavi has built new business units, led partnerships, fundraising, curriculum development, and program management.She holds a master’s degree in Development Engineering, a graduate certificate in Transforming Food Systems, and an undergraduate degree in Interdisciplinary Field Research from UC Berkeley. Kavi holds a Permaculture Design Certificate, advanced certificates in soil fertility building and landscape design, and is pursuing a permaculture diploma in community development. At the Soil Food Web Foundation, Kavi leads growth, partnerships, and permaculture programs to advance access to soil health and regenerative ecology education. Her passion is to catalyze relationships of reciprocity between humans, soil, and nature.

name: Evan Buckman
bio:
Evan Buckman is an entrepreneur, scientist, and regenerative systems thinker dedicated to transforming food systems, advancing regenerative agriculture, and healing humanity’s relationship to nature.

In 2014, Evan earned his Permaculture Design Certificate from the Finger Lakes Permaculture Institute, laying the foundation for his systems-based approach to ecological design. He went on to graduate from Minerva University in 2021 with a Bachelor of Science in Applied Chemistry, concentrating in Biological and Earth Systems. His senior thesis, “Systems Biology Approaches to Bioremediation,” explored nature’s innate capacity to restore balance and detoxify human-caused pollution. During his studies, he lived in seven cities around the world, gaining invaluable cultural experiences.

Evan began his entrepreneurial journey in 2015 and has since founded multiple ventures, including an organic restaurant, a nutritional supplement company, and a consulting firm supporting impact-driven, bioeconomy-focused enterprises. He is also an avid researcher, having studied and trained in fields including holistic health, mycology, traditional ecological knowledge, and interdisciplinary life sciences. Evan is committed to creating positive impact through his actions, and has contributed to philanthropic causes including providing clean water and sanitation access to rural and indigenous populations around the world, and developing regenerative bio-economies in the Amazon Rainforest.

He is currently based in Texas, where he moved to pursue large scale regenerative land projects. This led him to producing commercial bio-amendments and distributing them to landscapers, farmers, and land stewards to boost soil health and increase ecological resilience. He met Dr. Elaine Ingham through this work and has been inspired by the deep legacy and immense global impact of the Soil Food Web community. Evan has been working with Dr. Ingham, her family, and the Soil Food Web school team to develop the Soil Food Web Foundation as a vehicle to carry forward Elaine’s immense legacy and the Soil Food Web mission for future generations. He is honored to serve as the Executive Director of the Foundation and committed to promoting widespread human and planetary health by regenerating the living soils beneath our feet.

name: Leslie W. Lewis, Ph.D.
bio:
Leslie Lewis worked in higher education for almost four decades. After receiving her Ph.D. with a focus in the humanities, she taught widely at numerous institutions. Her later career focused on liberal arts education, and she supported the interdisciplinary humanities and sciences as Dean of the School of Humanities and Sciences at Ithaca College and Provost at Goucher College in Baltimore.

Leslie came to the study of soil health as an academic researcher and writer as well as a long- time organic grower. While teaching a course on regenerative farming, sustainability, and the food system, she met Elaine Ingham at a conference in 2020. This began her journey with the Soil Food Web school, including completing the microscopy and consulting programs.

Leslie is passionate about hands-on learning, and equally passionate about the pursuit of knowledge through research. Her early years on her family’s farm are her touchstone for real- world practicality and a deep well of commitment to regenerative agriculture and ecosystem restoration.

name: Jenna Noel
bio: Jenna Noel is the daughter of two pioneering microbiologists, Dr. Elaine Ingham and Dr. Russel Ingham. She has been steeped in soil science her whole life, having spent much of her summers as a child counting nematodes under the microscope and learning to make really good compost. In addition to a successful career in management, Jenna is a proud mother, sports enthusiast, and committed to the Soil Food Web Mission. She represents the Ingham family as an active steward of Dr. Elaine’s living legacy and the ongoing work to promote ecologically healthy food systems around the world.

name: Eric Feiler
bio: Eric graduated cum laude with a Bachelor’s Degree in Anthropology and Archeology from Colorado College. He later earned his Master of Science in Quaternary Studies with an emphasis in Paleoecology and Archeology, graduating with distinction. He served as Co-Founder and Board Member of the PaleoCultural Research Group before becoming the Property Manager for a 200-acre ecological restoration site in Boulder, Utah. Eric also owns High Desert Soil Works, LLC, where he does consulting and specialized compost production.

name: Stephanie McDaniel
bio:
An avid gardener and a student of the Soil Food Web School, she brings her more than 20 years of experience as a business owner and operator across food systems, online education, fintech, and community-based initiatives to the mission of soil regeneration. Her career focus is to help mission-driven organizations communicate clearly and operate better so they can grow impact without losing their values.

At the Soil Food Web Foundation, her work emphasizes community building, growth outreach, and long-term program sustainability in support of the Foundation’s mission of empowering individuals and organizations to regenerate soil in their communities.

name: Loida Vasquez
bio:
With a B.S. in Regenerative Agriculture and a specialized focus on living soils, Loida Vasquez brings deep expertise and a proven track report in transforming conventional agriculture through soil biology. Over the course of her career, Loida has helped transition thousands of acres of farmland to regenerative systems, working directly with farmers, consultants, and land stewards to implement practices rooted in soil health and ecological resilience.

Loida has learned from and worked closely with Dr. Elaine Ingham for decades, from Elaine’s time as the Chief Scientist at the Rodale Institute, to many years of dedication to the Soil Food Web school. As a leader in the field, Loida has designed and led dozens of workshops on composting, soil biology, and regenerative land management, empowering hundreds of practitioners with actionable, science-based methods. Her work emphasizes practical, biology-first approaches to land restoration and productivity.

With a blend of technical knowledge, hands-on experience, and leadership in education, Loida is committed to advancing regenerative agriculture at a scale through collaboration, innovation, and systems thinking.

name: Gerald Ramírez
bio:
Gerald Ramírez is an Agronomist who graduated from the University of Costa Rica and recently completed his licentiate thesis. Gerald serves as an instructor for CLP and CTP at the school, as well as contributing as a soil analyst in the interpretation of physical and chemical soil indicators for optimizing management practices, with a focus on soil health and sustainability. Additionally, he provides valuable insights into crop management.

Gerald initially joined the Soil Food Web School as a Content Developer but was later promoted to an Instructor role after completing Tier 3 Professional Development with the School. He still actively contributes to content creation, with his areas of expertise being applied mathematics, research, and transitional agriculture.

name: Dr. Carla Ribeiro Machado e Portugal
bio: Dr. Carla Ribeiro Machado e Portugal speaks Portuguese, English, and Spanish while working as a simultaneous translator/interpreter for Portuguese-English, and English-Portuguese. She began her academic career at the Federal University of Uberlândia, graduating in 2004. She then completed a Master’s in Environmental Engineering, relocated to the United States, and completed her Ph.D. in Environmental Sciences after researching the biostabilization of unpaved roads to minimize the impact of hydric erosion. Her research has resulted in 27 empirical listings. Since 2008, Dr. Portugal has served as a co-founder of a consultancy company in Brazil for Environment and Agriculture projects. She consulted with the Brazilian federal government in developing and approving one of the few Category II centers within UNESCO focused on Education for Water management for Portuguese-speaking countries. She also worked for the government of Minas Gerais developing strategies to enhance the abilities of small farmers and settlements to achieve better agricultural practices towards organic and sustainable practices. She served as Environmental Education Supervisor and Environmental Legislation Supervisor at Instituto Inhotim, a significant Botanical Garden in Brazil. Since 2019, Dr. Portugal has served as an Instructor, Mentor, Researcher, and Translator for the Soil Food Web School. Her robust skills consistently guide her international students toward success.

name: Dora Tkalec
bio:
Based in Tampere, Finland
A teacher by training and a gardener at heart. Her passion for growing healthy food and finding that divine taste of a ripe tomato from her childhood led her to the path of permaculture. There, she delved into the magical properties of compost and recognized the fundamental role of soil in functioning ecosystems. In 2019, when she moved to Finland with her family, she finally had the chance to join Dr. Elaine’s school. Since 2020, she has been working as a project manager, composting expert, and educator at an agricultural vocational school. She developed a composting process for the school’s dairy farm, taught students the magic of composting, and gave numerous courses and lectures to landscape professionals and gardeners alike through several EU and national projects. She has collaborated with several farms on developing composting processes and conducted successful trials in their own contexts. She is particularly interested in utilizing farms’ animal manure to create the perfect soil amendment, thereby optimizing the nutrient cycling on farms. She is convinced that understanding the complexity of natural systems and selfless human cooperation can lead humanity to the better world our hearts know is possible.

name: Nick Padwick
bio:
Nick, a Hampshire farm native, has become a prominent figure in sustainable agriculture. His early education at Sparsholt Agricultural College laid the groundwork for a career of innovation and excellence. Beginning with management roles in the Co-operative farms group, Nick quickly established a reputation for transformative agricultural practices.

In Leicestershire, Nick and his wife launched the award-winning Farm to Fork project, earning them the Unilever Social Intervention Award and underscoring Nick’s dedication to sustainable agriculture. This project cemented his status as a leader committed to responsible farming practices.

In 2009, Nick’s contributions to the field were recognized with Farmer’s Weekly’s Farm Manager and Farmer of the Year awards. He then moved to the South Pickenham Estate, where he managed 10,000 acres across multiple countries, showcasing his expertise in international agriculture.

In 2018, Nick took on the management of Ken Hill Estate, home to the nationally recognized Wild Ken Hill nature restoration and regenerative farming project. His leadership has transformed Ken Hill into a model of biodiversity and sustainable agriculture.

Through Peddar Farming, Nick oversees over 5,000 acres in West Norfolk, implementing practices that enhance soil health and support wildlife conservation. A graduate of the Soil Food Web and a Soil Laboratory Technician, Nick is on track to become one of the first Soil Food Web consultants in the UK.

Nick’s work has not only advanced countryside stewardship but has also set an example for farmers nationwide, demonstrating how stewardship schemes can be tailored to maximize productivity and environmental benefits. His career is a testament to visionary leadership in British farming, setting new standards for agricultural and environmental excellence.

name: Ib Borup Pedersen
bio: Ib is a Danish farmer. He has worked in farming all his life and owned his own farm for 20 years, with 110 ha arable land, 9 ha of which were organic strawberries and a 500-sow pig unit. Since 2017, Ib has been a farmer / teacher at a Danish boarding school for 9 and 10 graders, where he runs the school’s 43 ha organic farm. He teaches organic farming, both practice and theory, and SFW methods to his students. He has done extensive work on SFW field trials for the last five years, both at the school, where some of the work has been done by the students, and on nearby farms. During this time, he has gained experience of using the SFW system through studies in arable crops, grazing fields, forage fields, strawberries, orchards and greenhouses. He has a good technical background and is working on getting systems up and running that can easily be put in place on organic, as well as conventional farms. His aim is to get Soil Food Web solutions brought out to farmers and growers in a practical and cost-effective way. As well as consulting Farmers and growers, he also produces extractors, and other equipment that are all aimed at making SFW work easier and cost efficient.

name: Casey Williams
bio: Casey is an agriculture expert with extensive experience, both in theory and practical application, in the areas of permaculture, soil health, and regenerative farming. Over the years, Casey has worked in many capacities in agriculture, including managing farms, doing permaculture design, cultivating gourmet mushrooms and microgreens, building and running aquaponics systems, and producing biochar and compost. Being a certified consultant through the Soil Food Web School and running his business has allowed him to continue to promote regenerative land management through direct application, education, and hands-on mentorship. By constantly experimenting with different composting methods and biochar production methods at various scales, as well as learning diverse approaches to land stewardship, Casey continuously builds on his knowledge base in this complex field.

name: Brian Daubenspeck
bio: Since exiting his careers in mechanical engineering and management consulting, Brian has been producing food, working with farmers and closely observing the food system with the intention of healing and reconnecting the planet through agriculture. He has managed a variety of farms and ranches across the US and Latin America. It was while working with smallholder farmers in southern Mexico that Brian discovered the Soil Food Web School and in 2022, he graduated from the Consultant Training Program.

name: Wesley Sander
bio: Wesley Sander has spent most of his life around farming. Growing up, Wesley helped his family raise chickens, cows and pigs on a small acreage in northern California, USA. He earned a bachelor’s degree in journalism, with background study in biology, from Humboldt State University before spending the next decade writing for various publications on several subject areas, foremost among them agriculture. He reported on all aspects of the industry, including legislative and regulatory processes in the state Capitol; litigation over federal approval of genetically modified crops; conservation practices, scientific advances and field trials; and the policymaking surrounding labor, immigration, international trade and water rights. Wesley left journalism to spend the next decade managing a small farm in the Sierra Nevada foothills, where he began implementing Soil Foodweb techniques to great success. He now serves clients through his consultancy, Foothill Biological Soil Health Services, and since June 2020 has served as an Advanced Programs mentor at the Soil Food Web School.

name: Ayşen Üstünay
bio:
With 25 years in international trade, Ayşen Üstünay built a corporate career in Sales, Marketing, and Strategy.

Early health issues inspired a search for self-understanding and body awareness, leading her toward healthy nutrition. Despite an intense urban lifestyle, she maintained a strong connection to the soil, using every chance to grow her own food, which ultimately restored his health.

This personal transformation sparked a deeper curiosity about soil and health. After conventional sources fell short of providing answers, a footnote in a book led her to Dr. Elaine Ingham and Soil Food Web (SFW) training. Through SFW practices, she found the answers she sought and discovered the holistic cycle connecting soil, health, and all living things. This journey has transformed her worldview and continues to shape it.

She now sees working with microorganisms as a powerful, enjoyable, and distinctive approach for creating positive change in both personal and global health.

name: Isadora Shmidt
bio:
Isadora Shmidt has always felt somewhat a misfit, wandering through life until nature finally drew her in. Her first career didn’t fulfill her, but everything changed when she stumbled upon market gardening. Learning to grow vegetables was enjoyable, but then permaculture found her—and she discovered that people had already written books about what she’d been imagining! The challenge, however, was that she didn’t own land, and permaculture felt like a personal escape from modern life rather than a practical pursuit.

Determined to make a real impact, she dove into regenerative agriculture, where she uncovered something even more transformative: the Soil Food Web! Dr. Elaine Ingham’s work became a revelation—understanding soil is essential for making choices that lead to thriving ecosystems.

Today, she helps others discover the wonders of soil. Though she’s far from knowing it all (imposter syndrome, anyone?), she’s committed to asking questions, digging deeper, and guiding others with both confidence and humility. For her, regenerative agriculture isn’t only about land; it’s about people, too. She’s dedicated to supporting change with a spirit of respect, curiosity, and, when needed, a bit of humor.

name: Sammie Bass
bio: Samantha Bass was inoculated with the soil food web approach in January of 2017 while attending a 5-day workshop with Dr. Elaine Ingham. She implements biological farming practices on her ⅓ acre homestead and a 1-acre plot growing food for her family and friends. Since November 2019, she has served as the Soil Food Web School’s (SFWS) Marketing Associate, where she is a liaison between SFWS and various advertising agencies to ensure the digital marketing strategy and execution are performed flawlessly. Samantha’s academic background includes a Bachelor of Arts in Hospitality and Tourism Management with a minor in Economics. She began her career at the Better Business Bureau in San Diego. Later positions included Assistant Manager of Operations and Office Manager. Before joining SFWS, Samantha served as Board President for Nevada County Grown, coordinating publicity and marketing events for farmers and agritourism members throughout California’s Nevada County.

name: Delvin Solkinson
bio: Delvin Solkinson is a community gardener, student and teacher from British Columbia, Canada. Delvin co-created and ran a federally funded youth program called ‘Eco-Tech’ which built community gardens and school gardens. He built the ‘Heart Gardens’ surrounding his tiny coastal rainforest village downtown core based on plants with a history of use by Coastal First Peoples and including an eco-education centre, seed bank and farmers market. Completing a Permaculture Design Certificate, Diploma and Masters Degree with Bill Mollison, the co-originator of Permaculture, was part of his life long learning. Delvin has done many in-person programs including 13 advanced courses and 14 teacher trainings with Permaculture elders like David Holmgren, Rosemary Morrow, Geoff Lawton and Robin Clayfield. Ongoing training included three additional Permaculture Education Diplomas, numerous Permaculture Design Certificate Courses, and a Doctoral Degree with Larry Santoyo of the Permaculture Academy. Co-facilitating the Group Diploma Adventure with Looby Macnamara, he is a Diploma Tutor with Permaculture Association UK. Delvin serves as the Diploma Program Co-ordinator for the Permaculture Institute. He is also a Senior Diploma Tutor with Permakultur Danmark. Delvin recently served as Dean and Lead Instructor with his wife Grace for the Permaculture School at Pacific Rim College on a 720 hour in-person Permaculture Design and Resilient Ecosystems Diploma. They built gardens and structures, raised animals and led a large teaching team including Indigenous Wisdom Holders. Together they teach, write books, create card decks and learning games, write articles and serve as social media managers for Permaculture Magazine. Delvin collaborated with Dr. Elaine Ingham and the Soil Food Web School to co-create Graham Bell’s legacy online Permaculture Design Certificate featuring 74 teachers from 22 countries. He is a true believer in the ability of permaculture design to support people from all walks of life.

name: Alex Andreou
bio: Alexandros Andreou serves as the Information Technology Manager for SFWS. Alex served as a Cryptography Specialist in the military before becoming a Junior Developer and Web Designer. After only two years, he was recruited as the Head Developer for an advertising agency utilizing HTML, JavaScript, AJAX, and JSON coding to generate SEO best practices across all departments. He shortly began doing his own freelance work as a consultant for website development, custom plugins, network security, and streamlining business processes for greater efficiency. He also added hardware support to his skillsets by making computer upgrades, imaging new equipment, and matching hardware and software sophistication to the end user’s performance requirements. He brought his sixteen years of IT experience to the SFWS, where he serves as the Project Manager for all IT projects, is a strategic partner for the Executive Team, and manages all contract IT staff. Alex also facilitates all IT needs for our proprietary Learning Management System and integrated Student Management System. For example, rather than trusting a Third-Party application to meet IACET requirements, Alex is building those into the core of the LMS and integrating reporting through the Student Management System upgrade.

name: Elena Kalli
bio: Elena Kalli brings over 20 years of experience in business operations, strategic planning, and organizational development. Specializing in company culture and HR, she is dedicated to fostering purpose-driven workplaces and optimizing team dynamics. Her expertise lies in refining processes, solving complex challenges, and guiding organizations through critical transitions.Inspired by the transformative work of Soil Food Web, Elena is deeply committed to supporting mentors and students as they work toward their goals. She focuses on creating systems and processes that empower the community, ensuring they have the structure and guidance needed to succeed.Her experience spans multiple industries, including education, consulting, and corporate governance, where she has played a key role in streamlining operations and enhancing efficiency. At Soil Food Web, she helps drive meaningful improvements and supports the team in making a lasting impact.When she’s not focused on helping people grow, Elena enjoys staying active, spending time with her children, and attempting to win the affection of her cats.

name: Pranjal Rajput
bio: Pranjal Rajput is a technology innovator and environmental advocate bringing two decades of software engineering expertise to revolutionize how we understand and nurture soil ecosystems.With a Master’s in Information Technology from Indore University, Pranjal has architected transformative digital solutions for telecommunications, banking, and finance sectors across USA, Australia, UK, and Ireland. His technical leadership has been instrumental in shipping applications that serve millions of users globally, including a groundbreaking telco platform and the complete reinvention of a major bank’s wealth management system. A tinkerer at heart who stays hands-on with code, he has coached numerous organizations in startup culture, agile methodologies and strategic goal execution.Pranjal’s environmental awakening came through volunteering with The Nature Volunteers, a non-profit dedicated to preserving Central India’s wetlands. While documenting biodiversity through his lens, he discovered that every corner of nature teems with interconnected life – a revelation that sparked his lifelong commitment to understanding and protecting these intricate ecosystems. Coming from a farming family and carrying childhood memories of school holidays on ancestral farms, he has observed the universal struggles of conventional agriculture, from degraded soils to financial pressures – affecting farmers in both India and Australia. His frequent travels between his home base in Indore and Sydney, where he maintains significant business and investment interests, have given him unique insights into these parallel agricultural challenges across continents.At the Soil Food Web Foundation, Pranjal is pioneering AI-enabled solutions for soil microscopy and health management, weaving together artificial intelligence, IoT, blockchain, and remote sensing technologies to create breakthrough innovations for regenerative agriculture. He is spearheading the technical infrastructure to support the Foundation’s transformation into a global non-profit, enabling worldwide scaling and localization of Dr. Elaine Ingham’s crucial teachings. His mission is clear: in an era of climate crisis and soil degradation, humanity cannot afford to gamble with our only planet.Based between India and Sydney with his wife and two sons, Pranjal dreams of returning to his family’s farmland to practice the regenerative principles he champions. When not coding or strategizing, he can be found hiking with his camera, capturing nature’s intricate beauty, or occasionally unwinding with video games.
